title: Idlewild and other boats, Earl Humphrey leaving Desvigne
summary: Bill and Nelson describe the Idlewild stern wheeler, trips upriver as far as Memphis, and trombonist Humphrey who left for show travel.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I was going to ask some more about that Idlewild. I think I saw a picture, Idlewild or what? Well it didn't stay here long.
About as big as the capital?
No, not quite that large. Was it a side wheeler or back? No, back stern wheeler.
Made like the capital, not as large.
Yeah, big dance floor and all the other. Big dance floor and everything.

Then I went up the river one year on President out there now. We made a trip up there. For one year, didn't go no footer to St. Louis. Then we made a trip, I made a trip up the river with him on the Island of Queen. Well the weather was so bad we couldn't get no footer than Memphis. As far as he could go, it was too cold.
Is that the boat that went up the Ohio sometimes? That's the boat.
Well I wasn't with him when he was on that boat going to Cincinnati. See, he had a fellow by the name of Oil Umphrey. If you remember him. That's Willie Umphrey's brother.
He's a trombone player. Well the reason why he left Sydney, not to say his musical ability, he's a circus man. He likes to follow the shows. He don't stay in one place, he likes to travel.
He's over in Virginia now, someplace based.
I don't know. He does? Well I don't know, I couldn't tell you, I don't know where he passed. I couldn't tell you that.
No he's still there. His brother's over.
